# General Functions

In this section, we design some general-use functions which may find place in subroutines used in the building of more complex functions: - sums / higher moments - exponentiation - square root - log

We will also be using these functions as examples to show **techniques** that would be useful in other scenarios. Specifically: 

1. Exponentiation shows the power of **Taylor series**. 

2. The square root conveys the utility of **giving computation back to the user post-FHE**.

## Some Basics

We are allowed to generate encoded vectors of any constant, c. $$ct_c=enc(c_1, c_2, \dots,c_{N/2})$$ Note that $c_i$ can be distinct from $c_j$ This allows us to do computations with pre-computed constant vectors $$c*enc(z_*)=enc(c,c,\dots,c)*enc(z_*)=enc(cz_1,cz_2,\dots,cz_{N/2})$$ 
Since we have multiplication, it is easy to divide by *known constants*, since we can multiply by their inverse. Specifically, we can take $$\mathtt{enc}(z_*) * \mathtt{enc}(\frac{1}{c_*}) \rightarrow \mathtt{enc}(\frac{z_1}{c_1}, \ldots, \frac{z_{N/2}}{c_{N/2}})$$ by precomputing constants $1/c_*$ from $c_*$.

### Selection Vector (a.k.a. One-Hot, Masking, Binary Vector)

Suppose we want certain elements in our ciphertext. We can encrypt a vector of ones (selected) and zeros (not selected) to decide on which elements are needed. For example, if we wanted to take only the first element of our vector $ct=enc(z_1,z_2,\dots z_{N/2})$, all we need is one multiplication with our pre-encrypted $ct_0=enc(1,0,0,\dots0)$ to obtain $$ct_*=ct_0*ct=enc(1,0,0,\dots,0)*enc(z_1,z_2,\dots, z_{N/2})=enc(z_1,0,0,\dots,0)$$

### Efficient Exponentiation (Repeated Squaring)

Suppose we wanted to obtain $ct_{x^k}=enc(x_1^k, \ldots, x_{N/2}^k)$.

While we can naively obtain $(x_1^k, \ldots, x_{N/2}^k)$ in $O(k)$ time by repeated multiplication, it is faster to compute via the "fast squaring trick":

Let X be a ciphertext vector of length N/2.

$$X^2=X*X$$ (one operation)

$$X^3=X^2*X$$ (two operations)

$$X^4=X^2*X^2$$ (two operations)

$$X^5=X^2*X^3$$ (three operations)

$$X^6=X^3*X^3$$ (three operations) ... and so on.

Therefore, the 
$$ X \rightarrow X*X \rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow X * \cdots * X (k \text{ times}) $$ in $O(\log(k))$ operations.
